name: Semnani-Biyabuneki
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: semn1249 (Semnani-Biyabuneki) is not in the catalog. The single title-sweep item, Kolbitsch & Kolbitsch 2010 'The Thousand Accents' Island', is a Semnan-township dialect survey ('accents' = Persian lahje 'dialects'): Glottolog types it as an overview and the only scholarly use I could see (Hassanzadeh-Nodehi 2025) cites it for a five-way variety division; no online copy exists (Persian conference proceedings, print-only; searches via Crossref/OpenAlex/S2/Google Books/civilica/curl search engines found nothing) -> not a word-stress source, priority low. The sweep's real gain: the 2025 Frankfurt dissertation 'Towards a grammar of the Semnāni language' (CC-BY, previously blocked by the Anubis wall) was obtained from the Deutsche Nationalbibliothek archived copy (d-nb.info/1386474673/34) and saved with text and a page crop; its § 1.12 (p. 42) states final stress on simple nouns/adjectives/compounds with stressed verbal prefixes (na-, ma-/ba-, hā-/vā-/da-/dum-/dam-), unstressed direct-plural -i vs stressed oblique -un, vocative initial stress and stress-marked gender. This agrees with Christensen 1915 § 11 bis pp. 239-240 (final, 'comme en persan', same exceptions), Paxalina 1999 p. 145 and Rastorgueva 1999 p. 163 (Biyabuneki: last syllable), all read from files already on file. Recommended coding for a new catalog record: fixed final stress with morphologically conditioned exceptions; deciding source Hassanzadeh-Nodehi 2025 p. 42, corroborated by Christensen 1915. new_statements.quote: § 11 bis. Comme en persan, l’accent tonique repose, en général, sur la dernière syllabe d’un mot. Mais il y a des exceptions. Quant aux substantifs, l’i final, signe du cas oblique du singulier et du cas sujet du pluriel, ne reçoit pas d’accent (änǰíl „figue“, cas obl. änǰíli, cas sujet du pluriel de même). Si, au contraire, le cas oblique du singulier se termine en in, cette terminaison a l’accent (χarín, cas obl. de χar „âne“). La terminaison un du cas oblique du pluriel porte également l’accent (dutärún, de dutǻ „fille“). ... Les formes verbales qui n’ont pas de préfixe portent généralement l’accent sur la désinence ... Mais les préfixes mä, bä (bi), hå, vå, dä, du et la négation nä (ni) attirent l’accent
new_statements.translation: § 11 bis. As in Persian, the tonic accent rests, in general, on the last syllable of a word. But there are exceptions. As for nouns, the final -i, marker of the oblique case singular and of the direct case plural, does not receive the accent (änǰíl 'fig', obl. änǰíli, direct plural likewise). If, on the contrary, the oblique singular ends in -in, this ending has the accent (χarín, obl. of χar 'donkey'). The ending -un of the oblique plural likewise carries the accent (dutärún, from dutǻ 'daughter'). ... Verb forms that have no prefix generally carry the accent on the ending ... But the prefixes mä, bä (bi), hå, vå, dä, du and the negation nä (ni) attract the accent.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent is on the final syllable of the word, Persian-style. Morphological exceptions: the case ending -i (obl. sg. / direct pl.) is never accented (accent stays on the stem-final syllable), while obl. -in and obl.-pl. -un are accented; the old *-ak suffix (-a/-ä) is accented in some words but in others the accent has retracted to the penult (χarbī́zä 'melon', kiá 'house', bīčā́rä vs. tijärgä́ 'hail'); attributive-adjective -ä is atonic. In verbs, unprefixed forms accent the (last syllable of the) personal ending; the prefixes mä-, bä-/bi-, hå-, vå-, dä-, du- and negative nä-/ni- attract the accent (negation wins over another prefix: mänábu).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Prefixed verb forms have two accents, one on the prefix and one on the ending; usually the ending accent is barely audible, but when stem and ending fuse into one syllable (bǻšin, bǻšǻjn) the two are of nearly equal force and either may predominate; in mägämún, mägätún the final accent seemed the stronger. Paxalina 1999 p. 145 describes the same as main stress on the inflection with secondary stress on mê-/na-/preverb (mèbarún, mênàparsún).
new_statements.exceptions: Unaccented -i case ending; lexical penult accent in some *-ak nouns (χarbī́zä, kiá, bīčā́rä); atonic attributive -ä; enclitic postpositions (pi, gal, rä, nä), preverbal subject/object pronouns (unless emphatic; but hamǻ 'we', šamǻ 'you' always accented), some conjunctions (o, vä, ägä) and prepositions (äž, tå) are accentless. Christensen cautions (p. 230) that his accent rules are formulated 'sous toute réserve' from limited material; Shakibi Gilani 1990 p. XI reports accent-only minimal pairs (va↑ra 'snow' vs vara↑ 'lamb', the latter = Christensen's värrä́).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level: 'Chaque mot d'une phrase a son accent ou ses accents à lui'; accents were transcribed from dictated connected prose (texts) and elicited forms from a Semnan-town mīrzā, 1914. Variety: the town dialect of Semnan (sämnānī proper). Modern corroboration: Paxalina 1999 (Jazyki mira: Iranskie jazyki II, p. 145) states the same final-stress rule with unstressed obl.-sg. and direct-pl. -i and stressed verbal inflection; Rastorgueva 1999 pp. 149-150 gives final nominal stress for Biyabunaki and the other Semnan-strip dialects.
new_statements.identity_note: Christensen 1915 and Paxalina 1999 describe the town dialect of Semnan (sämnānī proper), which is the core of Glottolog semn1249 'Semnani-Biyabuneki' [smy]. Glottolog's languoid also subsumes Biyabunaki; Rastorgueva 1999 (same volume, pp. 149-150) treats Biyabunaki with Sorkhei/Lasgerdi/Aftari as 'Semnan-strip dialects' distinct from Semnani but reports the same final nominal stress for them. Christensen's appendix on Sängsarī (sang1350) and Lāsgirdī (lasg1238) concerns different glottocodes and was not used.

new_statements.quote: In general, a single morpheme noun receives the stress on the final syllable, for instance, uštur [uʃtʹur] "camel" (M.T/IC), oftov [oftʹov] "sun" (Š.Š/IC). Adjective takes the stress on the final syllable, such as kasin [kasʹin] "small" (S.R/OC). The negative prefix (na-) receives stress, such as naxurdim [nʹaxrdim] "we did not sleep" (M.T/IC). Aspectual prefixes such as ma- and ba- receive a primary stress, for instance, magitim [mʹagitim] "we took" (Š.Š/IC), bātun [bʹɑtun] "I said" (M.Ā/IC). Lexical prefixes (hā-, vā-, da-, dum-, dam-) receives stress, such as hagirim [hʹɑgirim] "we take" (M.Ā/IC).
new_statements.citation: Hassanzadeh-Nodehi, Ramin. 2025. Towards a grammar of the Semnāni language. Diss., Goethe-Universität Frankfurt / Sapienza Roma. doi:10.21248/gups.95064 (CC-BY 4.0; copy from https://d-nb.info/1386474673/34)
new_statements.locator: § 1.12 'Stress position in Semnāni', p. 42 (PDF p. 42); page image
new_statements.reading: Semnani has fixed word-final (ultimate) lexical stress on simple nouns, adjectives and compounds, Persian-type, with morphologically conditioned exceptions: verbal prefixes (negative na-, aspectual ma-/ba-, lexical preverbs hā-, vā-, da-, dum-, dam-) carry primary stress; the direct-plural suffix -i is unstressed (penultimate stress), the oblique-plural -un is stressed; vocatives shift stress to the initial syllable; masculine vs feminine nouns in -a/-ā/-i are distinguished by stressed vs unstressed final vowel. This 2025 corpus-based first-hand description agrees with Christensen 1915 § 11 bis ('comme en persan, l'accent tonique repose, en général, sur la dernière syllabe d'un mot', with the same prefix and -i/-un exceptions) and with Paxalina 1999 p. 145 and Rastorgueva 1999 p. 163 (Biyabuneki: last syllable, prefix stress in verbs). Proposed coding: fixed final stress (morphology-sensitive exceptions).

sources.quote: Ударение у имен, как правило, падает на последний слог слова: mirdaká 'мужчина', ǰaniká 'женщина', beré 'брат', dår(á) 'дерево', ruwá 'кошка'. Не принимают на себя ударения: 1) окончания косвенного падежа мужского и женского рода ед. числа (oštór-i sahíb 'хозяин верблюда', aspá-i badiám 'я увидел собаку'); 2) окончание прямого падежа мн. числа -i: píri 'сыновья', dári 'деревья' (ср. окончание косв. падежа мн. числа -ún: pirún 'сыновей, сыновьями' и т. д.). [tr.: Stress in nouns as a rule falls on the last syllable of the word ... Unstressed: oblique-sg. endings and direct-plural -i (vs. oblique-plural -ún).]

sources.note: p. 145 (sec. 5.1.0): 'Ударение у имен, как правило, падает на последний слог слова: mirdaká, ǰaniká, beré, dår(á), ruwá. Не принимают на себя ударения: 1) окончания косвенного падежа м. и ж. рода ед. числа (oštór-i sahíb, aspá-i badiám); 2) окончание прямого падежа мн. числа -i: píri, dǻri (ср. косв. мн. -ún: pirún). В глаголе в личных формах ударение, как правило, падает на флексию, но при наличии префикса длительности mê-, или отрицания na-, или какого-л. преверба появляется второстепенное ударение: mèbarún, dumèrižún, mênàparsún, dumèritán.'
